definitions: To fasten or secure something with a rope, string, or similar material.
To finish or complete a task, deal, or arrangement.
To occupy someone completely, making them unavailable.
To invest or commit money or assets so that they are not readily available for other uses.
To obstruct or block traffic or movement.
examples: Please tie up the boat securely.
We need to tie up all the loose ends before the deadline.
I'm tied up with meetings all morning.
Most of their capital is tied up in real estate.
The accident tied up traffic for hours.
